rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 is the best design (99.67), and the only clean isolated gain so far is ki. Iteration 4 moved ki 0.05 to 0.3 with nothing else changed and scored 64.1 to 97.2. Iteration 5 moved ki 0.3 to 0.5 with nothing else changed and gained a further 2.5, with oval progress up from 0.32 to 0.40. Every other change was confounded with at least one other variable and did not help. Iteration 3 cut speed and moved sensors (score fell). Iteration 4 in the candidate form also cut speed and changed sensor size.

Critique points accepted: (a) The draft changed kp (2.0 to 2.5) and base_speed (1.5 to 1.2) together, so the result could not be attributed. I drop both changes. (b) The draft's own diagnosis says max_error barely moves with kp, so the kp rise has no support. I keep kp at 2.0. (c) Speed cuts lowered progress in iteration 3 and cannot reach the 3 s finish. I keep base_speed at 1.5. (d) The draft's kd and sensor claims are not isolated, so I keep kd 0.25 and the iteration 5 sensors (0.012 m footprint, x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, y = 0.05 m). The critique's point that 0.008 m footprints narrow the outer range is accepted, so I do not adopt the iteration 6 candidate sensor change.

Partly accepted: the critique is right that ki gains may be small, so I test one further step rather than a large jump. ki 0.5 to 0.8 is the only change. At the +/-2 integral cap it raises the maximum integral contribution from 1.0 to 1.6 turn units (about 350 to 560 PWM), which is a moderate step.

Expected result: max_error on the oval at or below 0.06 (iteration 5: 0.0627), progress above 0.40, and line losses at 1 or fewer on the oval. Success threshold: both max_error and oval progress improve against iteration 5. Failure threshold: steering_oscillation above 0.16 with no max_error gain means the integral is overcorrecting, so the next step returns to ki 0.5. If the result is neutral, the offset-removal hypothesis has reached its useful limit and the next test should move to a different variable (kd alone).
